Guitarist Carmen Caramanica’s skills as a guitarist and teacher are legendary in Central New York. His versatility as a performer and musical director have enabled him to achieve success far beyond his home town of Utica, NY.
Carmen was interviewed at his studio in New Hartford, New York, on July 27, 2011, by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and I am off-camera at Carmen Caramanica’s studio in Utica, New York, and I’m very happy to have him here as a guest for the Jazz Archive at Hamilton College. Hey Carmen. We go back a long ways.
And I have to tell you that my graduate school, after I got out of Fredonia, was playing with you and Rick [Montalbano] and Dolores [Mancuso], and I forget the drummer’s name.
Joe DePalma. Of course he was Joey Dee, right?
